Passage: Phantom pain sensations are defined as perceptions experienced by an individual with respect to a limb or organ not physically present. Limb loss may result from amputation or congenital deficiency; however, phantom sensations may also follow nerve avulsion or spinal cord injury.
Question: is pain experienced in a missing body part or paralyzed area?

Passage: In mathematics, parity is the property of an integer's inclusion in one of two categories: even or odd. An integer is even when it is evenly divisible by two, and odd when it is not. For example, 6 is even because there is no remainder when it is divided by 2. By contrast, 3, 5, 7, and 21 each leave a remainder of 1 when divided by 2. Examples of even numbers include −4, 0, 82, and 178. In particular, zero is an even number. Some examples of odd numbers are −5, 3, 29, and 73.
Question: can an odd number be divided by an even number?

Passage: The liver is an organ charged with the detoxification and reduction of the various chemicals, poisons, and toxins which enter the body. For instance, ammonia, which is poisonous, is transformed by this organ into urea in fish, amphibians, and mammals; in birds and reptiles, however, it is converted into uric acid. The urea is then filtered by the kidney, being excreted as urine, or, in the case of fish and tadpoles, through the gills. Uric acid, being of a paste-like consistency, is expelled as a semi-solid waste, constituting the ``white'' in bird excrements. Moreover, the liver secretes bile, which the body employs to break down fats into usable fats and unusable waste.
Question: is the liver part of the excretory system?

Passage: Magnesium citrate is a magnesium preparation in salt form; it contains citric acid in a 1:1 ratio (1 magnesium atom per citrate molecule). The name ``magnesium citrate'' is ambiguous, and sometimes refers to other salts such as trimagnesium citrate, which has a magnesium:citrate ratio of 3:2.
Question: does magnesium citrate have citric acid in it?

Passage: A spark plug—sometimes called a sparking plug in British English, and colloquially a plug—is an apparatus employed to deliver electric current from an ignition system to the combustion chamber of a spark-ignition engine, for the purpose of igniting the compressed mixture of fuel and air by an electric spark, while containing the pressure of combustion within the engine. It possesses a metal threaded shell, electrically isolated from a central electrode by a porcelain insulator. The central electrode, which may contain a resistor, is connected by a heavily insulated wire to the output terminal of an ignition coil or magneto. The metal shell of the spark plug is screwed into the cylinder head of the engine, and is thus electrically grounded. The central electrode protrudes through the porcelain insulator into the combustion chamber, forming one or more spark gaps between the inner end of the central electrode and usually one or more protuberances or structures attached to the inner end of the threaded shell; these latter are designated the side, earth, or ground electrode(s).
Question: does a spark plug keep an engine running?

Passage: A lady may wear a long cloak, extending over the shoulders or to the ankles, which is commonly termed a cape; or she may wear a full-length cloak. A gentleman likewise wears a cloak of ankle-length or full-length. Cloaks of formal design are often furnished with costly linings and trimmings in colours, such as silk, satin, velvet, or fur.
Question: is a cape and a cloak the same?

Passage: Contour feathers are not evenly distributed upon the skin of the bird, save in certain groups such as the penguins, ratites, and screamers. In the majority of birds, the feathers spring from defined tracts of skin termed pterylae; between these tracts lie regions devoid of feathers, known as apterylae (or apteria). Filoplumes and down may spring from the apterylae. The arrangement of these feather tracts, termed pterylosis or pterylography, differs among bird families and has been employed in times past as a method for ascertaining the evolutionary affinities of avian families.
Question: do penguins have feathers arising from the epidermis?

Passage: A new engine is broken in by following certain prescribed driving directions during the first few hours of its service. The purpose of the breaking-in process concerns the contact between the piston rings and the cylinder wall. No universal preparation or fixed set of instructions exists for breaking in an engine. Of greatest importance, authorities disagree as to whether it is preferable to commence the engine's operation at high or low power for this purpose. Although there remain consequences to an unsuccessful break-in, these are more difficult to measure in modern engines than in older models. Generally, persons no longer break in the engines of their own vehicles after purchasing a car or motorcycle, because this process is performed during production. It is still common, even at the present time, to find that an owner's manual recommends gentle use at first, often specified as the first 500 or 1000 kilometres or miles. Yet it is usually only normal use without excessive demands that is specified, as opposed to limited or light use. The manual will, for example, state that the car be driven in a normal manner, but not in excess of the highway speed limit.
Question: do you need to break in a car?

Passage: Tomato purée consists of a thick liquid, prepared by cooking and straining tomatoes. The distinction between tomato paste, tomato purée, and tomato sauce lies in their consistency; indeed, tomato purée possesses a thicker consistency and a more profound flavour than sauce.
Question: is pureed tomatoes the same as tomato sauce?

Passage: The English system of spelling represents vowel sounds, in the main, by the five conventional letters ⟨a, e, i, o, u⟩, together with ⟨y⟩, which, depending upon context, may act as a consonant. Notwithstanding, apart from abbreviations, there are a small number of words in English that contain no vowels; this arises either because the vowel sounds are not denoted by vowel letters, or because the words are pronounced without any vowel sounds.
Question: can there be a word without a vowel?

Passage: The turkey vulture, likewise termed the turkey buzzard in certain North American regions and the John crow or carrion crow in parts of the Caribbean, constitutes the most widespread of the vultures of the New World. Being one of three species within the genus Cathartes of the family Cathartidae, it extends its range from southern Canada to the southernmost extremity of South America. It is found in a variety of open and semi-open habitats, encompassing subtropical forests, shrublands, pastures, and deserts.
Question: is there such a thing as a turkey vulture?

Passage: Many martial arts employ common objects as weapons; Filipino martial arts, such as Eskrima, include practice with machetes, canes, bamboo spears, and knives, as a result of the 333 year Spanish colonization of the Philippines, which prohibited the ownership and use of standard swords and bladed weapons; Chinese martial arts and some Korean martial arts commonly feature the use of improvised weapons, such as fans, hammers, and staves. There are even some western martial arts that are based on improvised weapons, as, for instance, British quarterstaff fighting and Irish stick fighting.
Question: can a hammer be used as a weapon?

Passage: The Himalayan range possesses many of the Earth's highest peaks, among which is Mount Everest, the highest; it includes, moreover, over fifty mountains exceeding 7,200 metres (23,600 ft) in elevation, including ten of the fourteen 8,000-metre peaks. By contrast, the highest peak outside Asia, Aconcagua in the Andes, stands at 6,961 metres (22,838 ft).
Question: is mount everest a part of the himalayas?

Passage: Radio waves constitute a species of electromagnetic radiation, possessing wavelengths in the electromagnetic spectrum that exceed those of infrared light. Their frequencies range from 300 gigahertz (GHz) down to 30 hertz (Hz). At 300 GHz, the corresponding wavelength is 1 mm; at 30 Hz, it is 10,000 km. In common with all other electromagnetic waves, radio waves travel at the speed of light. They are generated by electric charges that undergo acceleration, such as time-varying electric currents. Naturally occurring radio waves are emitted by lightning and by astronomical objects.
Question: do radio waves travel at the speed of light?

Passage: An acute triangle is a triangle wherein all three angles are acute, each measuring less than 90°. An obtuse triangle, by contrast, has one obtuse angle—that is, an angle greater than 90°—and two acute angles. Owing to the fact that the sum of the angles in a triangle must equal 180°, it is impossible for any triangle to possess more than one obtuse angle.
Question: do all triangles have at least two acute angles?

Passage: The University of Mary Hardin--Baylor (UMHB) is a Christian co-educational institution of higher learning situated at Belton in the State of Texas. UMHB was chartered by the Republic of Texas in 1845 as Baylor Female College, which constituted the female department of what is now Baylor University; it has since become an independent institution, grown to 3,914 students, and confers degrees at the baccalaureate, master's, and doctoral levels. The University is affiliated with the Baptist General Convention of Texas.
Question: is baylor and mary hardin baylor the same school?

Passage: Tyrannosaurus is a genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur. The species Tyrannosaurus rex (rex meaning ``king'' in Latin), which is often colloquially referred to as T. rex or T-Rex, represents one of the most completely known among the large theropods. The genus inhabited the region now known as western North America, which during that epoch formed an island continent termed Laramidia; its distribution was notably wider than that of other tyrannosaurids. Fossils are recovered from various rock formations of the Maastrichtian age, belonging to the upper Cretaceous Period, which span from 68 to 66 million years ago. It constituted the last recognized member of the tyrannosaurids, and was among the final non-avian dinosaurs to persist prior to the Cretaceous--Paleogene extinction event.
Question: are t rex and tyrannosaurus rex the same?

Passage: Typically, once spun, cotton candy is marketed only by colour. Lacking a clear name other than 'blue', the distinctive taste of the blue raspberry flavour mix has, in time, become a compound flavour that some other foods (gum, ice cream, rock candy, fluoride toothpaste) occasionally borrow (``cotton-candy flavored ice cream'') so as to evoke the nostalgia of cotton candy, which people are usually able to experience only on vacation or holidays. Pink bubble gum underwent a similar transition from a specific branded product to a generic flavour that transcended the original confection, and 'bubble gum flavour' is often found in the same product categories as 'cotton candy flavour'.
Question: do blue and pink cotton candy taste the same?

Passage: A floating island is a mass of aquatic vegetation, mud, and peat, ranging in thickness from several centimetres to a few metres. It is a common natural phenomenon, found in many regions of the world, though it exists less commonly as a product of human contrivance. Floating islands are generally situated upon marshlands, lakes, and similar wetland locations, and may extend over many hectares in area.
Question: is there such a thing as a floating island?

Passage: For the left side of the body, no brachiocephalic artery exists; the left common carotid and the left subclavian artery arise directly from the aortic arch. There are, however, two brachiocephalic veins.
Question: is there a right and left brachiocephalic artery?

Passage: The German Shepherd, a breed of medium to large-sized working dog, originated in Germany; its German name is Deutscher Schäferhund. In the English language, the breed's officially recognized name is German Shepherd Dog, though it is sometimes abbreviated as GSD. In Britain and Ireland, it is known as the Alsatian. The German Shepherd is a relatively new breed, with its origin dating to 1899. As a member of the Herding Group, the breed was developed originally for herding sheep. Since that time, however, by reason of its strength, intelligence, trainability, and obedience, the German Shepherd has become the preferred breed for a great many types of work, including disability assistance, search-and-rescue, police and military roles, and even acting. It is the second-most registered breed by the American Kennel Club and the seventh-most registered by The Kennel Club in the United Kingdom.
Question: is a german shepard the same as an alsatian?

Passage: Though certain experiments conducted in the 19th century put forward that the common assumption holds true provided the heating is sufficiently gradual, modern biologists maintain that the premise is false: a frog that is gradually heated will jump out. Indeed, the practice of thermoregulation by changing location constitutes a fundamentally necessary survival strategy for frogs and other ectotherms.
Question: does a frog jump out of boiling water?

Passage: As a unit of culinary measure, the level dessertspoon (dstspn.) is equivalent to two teaspoons, or 10 milliliters; whereas a U.S. tablespoon amounts to three teaspoons (15ml or half a fluid ounce) in the U.S., and two dessertspoons, that is to say four teaspoons (20ml or two thirds of a fluid ounce) in Britain and Australia, which latter adheres to the old British standard. For dry ingredients, a rounded or heaped teaspoonful is often specified instead.
Question: is a tablespoon bigger than a dessert spoon?

Passage: The White House serves as the official residence and workplace of the President of the United States; situated at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW in Washington, D.C., it has been the dwelling of every U.S. President since John Adams in 1800. The appellation is often employed as a metonym for the President and his advisers.
Question: does the president live in the white house?

Passage: The dorsal root ganglion, also known as the spinal ganglion or posterior root ganglion, constitutes a cluster of neurons—a ganglion—within the dorsal root of a spinal nerve. In this ganglion are situated the cell bodies of sensory neurons, termed first-order neurons.
Question: does the dorsal root ganglion carry sensory input?

Passage: Angular frequency, also known as angular speed, constitutes the magnitude of the vector quantity angular velocity. The term angular frequency vector ω → (\displaystyle (\vec (\omega ))) is occasionally employed as a synonym for the vector quantity angular velocity.
Question: is angular frequency and angular velocity the same?

Passage: Bullets discharged into the air typically descend at terminal velocities far below their muzzle velocity upon leaving the barrel of a firearm. Notwithstanding, injury, and sometimes death, may result when such bullets fall back to earth. Those fired at angles less than vertical are more perilous, as the projectile maintains its angular trajectory and is less prone to tumbling; it consequently travels at speeds greatly exceeding those of a bullet in free fall.
Question: can someone die from a bullet shot in the air?

Passage: The island is dominated by a maritime climate, with quite narrow temperature differences between seasons. Politically, Great Britain is part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, and constitutes most of its territory; most of England, Scotland, and Wales are on the island. The term ``Great Britain'' is often used to include the whole of England, Scotland, and Wales, including their component adjoining islands, and is also occasionally but contentiously applied to the United Kingdom as a whole in some contexts.
Question: is northern ireland part of the great britain?

Passage: The Catholic Church holds that the effects of the sacrament are as follows: As the sacrament of Marriage confers grace for the married state, so the sacrament of Anointing of the Sick imparts grace for the state into which persons enter upon sickness. Through this sacrament, a gift of the Holy Spirit is bestowed, which restores confidence and faith in God, and fortifies against temptations to discouragement, despair, and anguish at the thought of death and the struggle of dying; it hinders the believer from forfeiting Christian hope in God's justice, truth, and salvation. Inasmuch as one of the effects of the sacrament is to absolve the recipient of any sins not previously absolved through the sacrament of penance, solely an ordained priest or bishop is permitted to administer the sacrament.
Question: can anyone give last rites in an emergency?

Passage: Though it is a common practice, the removal of one's letter from the letter jacket upon graduation cannot be regarded as a firmly established protocol. Many graduates retain the letter upon the jacket after graduation as a symbol of accomplishment, school pride, and commitment; this is especially the case with college lettermen.
Question: can you wear your letterman after high school?

Passage: Powdered milk, also termed dried milk, is a manufactured dairy product obtained by evaporating milk to dryness. One purpose of drying milk is its preservation; milk powder possesses a far longer shelf life than liquid milk and requires no refrigeration, owing to its low moisture content. Another purpose is the reduction of its bulk for the economy of transportation. Among the items included in powdered milk and dairy products are dry whole milk, nonfat (skimmed) dry milk, dry buttermilk, dry whey products, and dry dairy blends. Many dairy products that are exported conform to the standards set forth in the Codex Alimentarius. Many forms of milk powder are subject to trade upon exchanges.
Question: is powdered milk the same as milk powder?

Passage: The Federal Government of the United States, also designated as the U.S. Federal Government, constitutes the national government of that country; it is a federal republic in North America, composed of 50 states, one district--Washington, D.C.--and several territories. This government is divided into three distinct branches: legislative, executive, and judicial, the powers of which are vested by the U.S. Constitution in Congress, the President, and the federal courts, respectively. The powers and duties of these branches are further defined by acts of Congress, including the creation of executive departments and courts inferior to the Supreme Court.
Question: does the united states have a federal system of government?

Passage: By definition, the parent-in-law is a person who stands in legal affinity with another by reason of being the parent of that person's spouse; a great many cultures and legal systems impose duties and responsibilities upon persons so connected. A son-in-law or daughter-in-law is related to the parents of the spouse, who are in turn the parents of those sisters-in-law and brothers-in-law (if any) who are siblings of the spouse, as opposed to the spouses of siblings. The whole of these relations are collectively termed the in-laws.
Question: is a father in law considered a relative?

Passage: A public limited company, abbreviated to plc, is a form of public company as provided for by the company law of the United Kingdom, certain Commonwealth jurisdictions, and the Republic of Ireland. It is a limited liability company, the shares of which may be freely sold and traded to the public; though a plc may also be privately held, often by another plc, it requires a minimum share capital of £50,000 and is usually designated by the letters PLC after its name. In the United States, similar companies are known as publicly traded companies. Public limited companies also possess a separate legal identity.
Question: are public limited companies in the private sector?

Passage: Temples, houses, bridges, and roads were destroyed; it is believed that nearly all buildings in the city of Pompeii were affected. In the days following the earthquake, anarchy prevailed in the city, and theft and starvation beset the survivors. During the interval from 62 to the eruption of 79, some rebuilding was undertaken, yet certain damage remained unrepaired at the time of the catastrophe. Although the exact number is unknown, a considerable portion of the inhabitants removed to other cities within the Roman Empire, while others stayed and rebuilt.
Question: were there any survivors in the pompeii eruption?

Passage: The heat of vaporization is dependent upon temperature; although, for small ranges and where the reduced temperature T r (\displaystyle T_(r)) ≪ 1 (\displaystyle \ll 1), a constant value may be assumed. It diminishes as the temperature rises, and vanishes entirely at the critical temperature ( T r = 1 (\displaystyle T_(r)=1) ); beyond this point, the liquid and vapor phases are indistinguishable, and the substance is termed a supercritical fluid.
Question: does latent heat of vaporization change with temperature?

Passage: Anosmia denotes an inability to perceive odour, or a lack of functioning olfaction; it is, in short, the loss of the sense of smell. This condition may be temporary, but certain forms, such as those arising from an accident, can be permanent. Anosmia is due to a number of factors, including inflammation of the nasal mucosa, blockage of the nasal passages, or destruction of one temporal lobe. Inflammation results from chronic mucosal changes in the paranasal sinus lining and in the middle and superior turbinates.
Question: is it possible to have no sense of smell?

Passage: Denatured alcohol, which serves as a solvent and as fuel for alcohol burners and camping stoves, has been employed for a great many additives and denaturing methods, owing to the diversity of its industrial uses; the principal additive has, traditionally, been 10% methanol, whence the term ``methylated spirits''. Among other common additives are isopropyl alcohol, acetone, methyl ethyl ketone, methyl isobutyl ketone, and denatonium.
Question: is denatured alcohol and acetone the same thing?

Passage: In mathematics, the dot product, or scalar product, is an algebraic operation which requires two sequences of numbers of equal length, commonly coordinate vectors, and produces a single number. In Euclidean geometry, the dot product of the Cartesian coordinates of two vectors is employed with great frequency and is often denominated the inner product, or, in rare instances, the projection product; reference may also be made to inner product space.
Question: is the dot product of two vectors a scalar?

Passage: Ocular dominance, sometimes termed eye preference or eyedness, denotes the tendency to prefer the visual input of one eye over that of the other. It bears a certain analogy to the laterality of right- or left-handedness; the side of the dominant eye, however, does not always correspond with that of the dominant hand. This circumstance arises because both hemispheres control both eyes, each taking charge of a different half of the field of vision and therefore a different half of both retinas (See Optic Tract for further particulars). No direct analogy between ``handedness'' and ``eyedness'' as lateral phenomena can thus be established.
Question: is there such thing as a dominant eye?

Passage: The navel, which is clinically termed the umbilicus and commonly referred to as the belly button or tummy button, constitutes a hollowed or, in certain instances, raised area upon the abdomen at the point of attachment for the umbilical cord. It is to be observed that all placental mammals are furnished with a navel.
Question: is navel and belly button the same thing?

Passage: The ensuing tables enumerate the names and symbols of cardinal numbers from 0 to 10 in various languages and writing systems throughout the world. Where practicable, the native script of each language is employed, together with transliterations in Latin characters and other significant scripts as applicable. In certain languages, the numerals are shown as far as 20.
Question: do numbers look the same in all languages?

Passage: Trees exhibit a wide variety of sizes, shapes, and growth habits. Specimens may grow as individual trunks, multitrunk masses, coppices, clonal colonies, or even more exotic tree complexes. Most champion-tree programmes focus upon finding and measuring the largest single-trunk example of each species. There are three basic parameters commonly measured to characterise the size of a single-trunk tree: height, girth, and crown spread. Further details on the methodology of tree-height measurement, tree-girth measurement, tree-crown measurement, and tree-volume measurement are presented in the links herein. A detailed guideline to these basic measurements is provided in The Tree Measuring Guidelines of the Eastern Native Tree Society by Will Blozan.
Question: can a tree have more than one trunk?

Passage: As an approximation of some merit for the square root of two, having a denominator of reasonable smallness, the fraction 99/70 (≈ 1.4142857) is sometimes employed.
Question: can root 2 be written as a fraction?

Passage: The pitaya, or pitahaya, is the fruit of several cactus species indigenous to the Americas; the term pitaya ordinarily denotes fruit of the genus Stenocereus, whereas pitahaya, or dragon fruit, designates fruit of the genus Hylocereus, both belonging to the family Cactaceae. Dragon fruit is cultivated in Southeast Asia, Florida, the Caribbean, Australia, and throughout tropical and subtropical regions.
Question: is dragon fruit and pitaya the same thing?

Passage: The chill-coma temperature, in the case of flying insects, is the temperature at which the flight muscles cannot be activated. In comparison with honey bees and carpenter bees, bumblebees possess the lowest chill-coma temperature; of these, Bombus bimaculatus exhibits the minimum, at 7 °C (45 °F). Nevertheless, bumblebees have been observed to fly in colder ambient temperatures. This discrepancy is to be ascribed to the fact that the chill-coma temperature was determined by means of tests conducted in a laboratory setting. However, bumblebees inhabit insulated shelters and are able to shiver in order to warm themselves before venturing into the cold.
Question: is a bumble bee the same as a carpenter bee?

Passage: A routing number is composed of a five digit transit number—also denominated the branch number—which designates the branch at which an account is held, and a three digit financial institution number pertaining to the financial institution. This number is set forth in one of the following forms, where XXXXX represents the transit number and YYY the financial institution number:
Question: is the routing number the same as transit number?

Passage: Because the courts of appeals are invested only with appellate jurisdiction, they do not hold sessions for trial. Courts possessing alone original jurisdiction conduct trials and thereby ascertain punishments in criminal cases and remedies in civil cases. In lieu thereof, appeals courts examine the decisions of trial courts for errors of law. Accordingly, an appeals court confines itself to the record; that is, the documents filed by the parties, the transcripts, and any exhibits from the trial, as well as the legal arguments presented by the parties. These arguments, which are submitted in writing and may range from dozens to hundreds of pages, are termed briefs. Occasionally, lawyers are permitted to supplement their written briefs by oral arguments before the appeals judges. At such hearings, only the lawyers of the parties address the court.
Question: does the us court of appeals have original jurisdiction?

Passage: A fried egg constitutes a cooked dish, prepared from one or more eggs extracted from their shells and placed into a pan—usually without rupture of the yolk—and fried with but slight accompaniment. Fried eggs are, by tradition, consumed at breakfast in a great many countries, though they may be served at other hours of the day as well.
Question: does a fried egg have a runny yolk?

Passage: This waterway permits passage from the Atlantic Ocean to the inland port of Duluth upon Lake Superior, a distance of 2,340 miles (3,770 km); and likewise to Chicago upon Lake Michigan, at a distance of 2,250 miles (3,620 km).
Question: can you boat from lake michigan to atlantic ocean?

Passage: Naval Base San Diego, known to inhabitants as 32nd Street Naval Station, constitutes the second largest surface-ship establishment of the United States Navy, and is situated at San Diego, California; it serves as the principal homeport of the Pacific Fleet, comprising upwards of 50 vessels and more than 190 subordinate commands. The establishment comprises 13 piers extending over 977 acres (3.95 km) of land and 326 acres (1.32 km) of water; the total population upon the base exceeds 24,000 military personnel and 10,000 civilians.
Question: is there a military base in san diego?

Passage: When an athlete is awarded a letter, or letters in multiple sports, and subsequently receives their letter, such an athlete is said to have ``lettered''.
Question: can you get more than one varsity letter?

Passage: It is commonly held that a worker honey bee is capable of stinging but once; this notion, however, is only partially correct. The stinger, being barbed, lodges in the skin of the victim and is torn from the bee's abdomen, leading to its death within minutes; yet this consequence follows only when the skin is of considerable thickness, as in mammals. Among the hymenoptera, the honey bee alone has a strongly barbed sting, whereas yellow jackets and some other wasps possess barbs of smaller size.
Question: do bees die if they lose their stinger?

Passage: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, or the Tomb of the Unknowns, is a monument set apart in memory of United States service members who have died without their remains being identified. Having no officially designated name, it is situated in Arlington National Cemetery, in the Commonwealth of Virginia, United States of America. The World War I ``Unknown'' is a recipient of the Medal of Honor, the Victoria Cross, and the highest service awards of several other nations. The United States Unknowns who have been interred are likewise recipients of the Medal of Honor, which was presented by the Presidents of the United States who presided over their funerals.
Question: are there actual bodies in the tomb of the unknown soldier?

Passage: A pickled cucumber is termed a pickle in the United States and Canada, and a gherkin in Britain, Ireland, Australia, South Africa, and New Zealand; it is a cucumber which has been pickled in brine, vinegar, or a similar solution and left to ferment, either by immersion in an acidic solution or through lacto-fermentation. It is common for such cucumbers to be included among mixed pickles.
Question: is a pickle the same as a gherkin?

Passage: Stenotype keyboards permit the trained user to input text at speeds of 225 wpm or more with great accuracy over an extended period; such proficiency suffices for real-time activities, as in court reporting or closed captioning. Although the rates of withdrawal are exceedingly high—in certain instances, only 10% or even less graduate—students of stenotype generally attain speeds of 100--120 wpm within six months, a pace surpassing that of most alphanumeric typists. According to Guinness World Records, the greatest speed achieved by means of a stenotype is 360 wpm with an accuracy of 97.23%.
Question: is it possible to type 200 words per minute?

Passage: Notwithstanding its heavy body and slow metabolism, the alligator is possessed of the capacity for short bursts of speed, and especially in brief lunges. The principal prey of the alligator consists of smaller animals, which it may dispatch and devour with a single bite. Larger prey may be seized and drawn into the water, to be drowned. Should any portion of the animal prove too great to be consumed in one instance, the alligator will either permit it to putrefy, or will bite and then spin or convulse violently, until pieces of a size suitable for eating are torn away. This action is termed a ``death roll''. A necessary condition for the alligator to commence this death roll is the flexion of its tail to a considerable angle in relation to its body. If the tail be immobilised, the alligator is unable to perform a death roll.
Question: do alligators drown their prey and eat it later?

Passage: More than 56% of the dust which fertilizes the Amazon rainforest is derived from the Bodélé depression of Northern Chad, situated in the Sahara desert. This dust contains phosphorus, a substance essential to plant growth; and the annual supply of Saharan dust replaces the equivalent quantity of that mineral which is yearly washed from Amazon soils by rains and floods. Upwards of 50 million tonnes of this dust are borne across the Atlantic Ocean each year.
Question: does the sahara desert in northern africa help south americas amazon rainforest grow?

Passage: A standard home blow dryer, when employed with due care, is capable of destroying 96.7% of the eggs. To be effective, the instrument must be applied repeatedly—every 1 to 7 days, as the eggs hatch within 7 to 10 days—until the natural life cycle of the lice, which lasts about 4 weeks, has been completed.
Question: can the heat of a hair dryer kill lice?

Passage: The Three Little Pigs is a fable concerning three pigs who construct houses of differing materials. A great bad wolf demolishes the first two houses, made of straw and sticks respectively, yet is unable to destroy the third, which is built of bricks. Printed versions are known from the 1840s, though the tale itself is believed to be of much greater antiquity. The phrases employed in the story, together with the various morals derived from it, have become deeply embedded in Western culture. Many versions of The Three Little Pigs have been recreated or modified over the years, sometimes portraying the wolf in a kindly character. It is classified as a type 124 folktale within the Aarne--Thompson system.
Question: is the three little pigs a nursery rhyme?

Passage: Maple syrup is a syrup prepared principally from the xylem sap of the sugar maple, the red maple, or the black maple, though other species of maple may also be employed. In cold climates, these trees store starch within their trunks and roots before winter; the starch is then converted to sugar, which rises in the sap during late winter and early spring. The trees are tapped by means of holes drilled in their trunks, and the exuded sap is collected; this sap is subsequently processed by heating, which serves to evaporate much of the water, leaving behind the concentrated syrup.
Question: does maple syrup come straight from the tree?

Passage: Although Robert Hooke's discovery of cells in 1665 led to the proposal of the Cell Theory, Hooke gave rise to the mistaken belief that all cells contained a hard cell wall, since only plant cells could be observed at the time. Microscopists focused upon the cell wall for well over 150 years, until advances in microscopy were made. In the early 19th century, cells were recognised as being separate entities, unconnected and bound by individual cell walls, after it was found that plant cells could be separated. This theory was extended to include animal cells, to suggest a universal mechanism for cell protection and development. They are produced during embryonic development in a process termed myogenesis.

Passage: During the 1770s, blacks throughout New England commenced sending petitions to the legislatures of the northern states, wherein they demanded freedom. Five of the Northern states, which had declared their independence, adopted policies for the gradual abolition of slavery: Pennsylvania (1780), New Hampshire and Massachusetts (1783), Connecticut and Rhode Island (1784). Vermont had abolished slavery in 1777, while it was still an independent state; and upon its admission to the United States as the 14th state in 1791, it was the first to join the Union untainted by the institution. These state jurisdictions, therefore, enacted the first laws for abolition in the Americas. By 1804 (including New York (1799), New Jersey (1804)), all of the northern states had abolished slavery or instituted measures for its gradual extinction.

Passage: In the game of ice hockey, a goal is reckoned to have been scored when the puck has wholly crossed the goal line between the two posts and below the crossbar. One point is awarded to the team upon whose goal the score is made, irrespective of the team to which the player who actually deflected the puck belongs (cf. own goal). In the usual course, a player upon the attacking side drives the puck with his stick towards the opening of the net, whereupon a player of the opposing side, known as the goaltender, endeavours to block the shot and so prevent a score against his own team.
